body_ar:
الوسوسة في العقيدة

ما حكم من يتعرض لوساوس الشيطان في عقيدته؟ بما ذا ينصح؟

على الإنسان إذا أحس بشيء من وسوسة الشيطان في اعتقاده أن يعلم أن ذلك من خطوات الشيطان التي نهانا الله تعالى عن اتباعها فقد قال الله تعالى:﴿يأيها الذين آمنوا لا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان﴾ . و عليه أن يكثر من ذكر الله تعالى فإن ذلك يطرد الشيطان فليكثر من الإستغفار و ليقل \"لا إله إلا الله\" فهذا يقطع على الشيطان السبيل و يزيل تلك الوساوس بالكلية و عليه أن لا يتبع التفكير التفكير، إذا جاءت فكرة خاطرة عليه أن لا يرددها، بل يقطعها بذكر الله تعالى...

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

بما تثبت العقيدة وأصول الدين؟

هل تثبت العقيدة وأصول الدين بخبر الآحاد؟

أن خبر الآحاد أربعة أنواع لدى أهل الحديث، القسم الأول منه المستفيض وهو الذي يقترب من المتواتر والفصل بينهما شاق وهذا تثبت به العقائد بدون خلاف، القسم الثاني المشهور وهو الذي رواه عدد في كل طبقة لا يزيدون على العشرة ولا ينقصون عن الثلاثة أو الأربعة، ثم يليه العزيز وهو الذي انفرد به في طبقة من الطبقات اثنان أو ثلاثة، ثم يليه الغريب وهو الذي انفرد به واحد في طبقة من الطبقات في أي طبقة من طبقاته،

وهذه الثلاثة اختلف فيها الناس هل تقتضي القطع أم لا، فذهب جمهور الأصوليين إلى أن خبر الآحاد إذا كان مشهورا أو عزيزا أو غريبا لا يقتضي القطع، وذهب المحققون منهم إلى أنه يقتضي القطع إن احتف بالقرائن التي تدل عليه، وذهب آخرون إلى أنه يقتضي القطع مطلقا وروي هذا عن جمهور أهل الحديث، ولكن القول الصحيح أن أخبار الآحاد إن احتفت بالقرائن اقتضت القطع ويمثل لذلك أهل الحديث بما يرويه مالك عن نافع عن ابن عمر عن رسول الله (ص)، فإنه يقتضي القطع لما احتف به من القرائن،

وعلى هذا الخلاف اختلف في الاستدلال بأخبار الآحاد في العقائد، والعقائد تنقسم إلى قسمين ما يطلب فيه القطع وهو أصول العقائد والديانات، وما لا يطلب فيه القطع وهو تفاصيلها، كتفصيل صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى ونحو ذلك، فتفاصيل الصفات على الراجح لا يشترط فيها القطع ولذلك يقبل فيها أخبار الآحاد، فيمكن أن تثبت صفة لله عز وجل بخبر الآحاد ويمكن أن يثبت له الاسم بذلك،

ولهذا يقول السيوطي رحمه الله: أسماؤه سبحانه موقفة** ثالثها الاسم فقط دون الصفه ويكتفى بمرة والمصدر** والفعل والظنون في المعتبر الظنون أخبار الآحاد،

أما الأمور القطعية والأصول أصول الديانات فلا بد فيها من القطع، فعلى القول بأن خبر الآحاد يفيد القطع مطلقا فلا إشكال في ثبوتها بذلك، وعلى القول بأنه يفيد القطع إن احتف بالقرائن فكذلك مثل ما رواه البخاري في الصحيح أو رواه مسلم في الصحيح حتى لو كان غريبا أو عزيزا فإنه احتف به من القرائن ما يقتضي القطع به، وإن شرط فيها القطع فإنه لا يؤخذ فيها بخبر الآحاد،

وحكمنا بالصحة على ما في الصحيحين لا يقصد به القطع عند الأصوليين وإنما يقصد به القطع عند المحدثين فقط، ولهذا قال العراقي رحمه الله في ألفية المصطلح: وبالصحيح والضعيف قصدوا** في ظاهر لا القطع والمعتمد إمساكنا عن حكمنا على سند** بأنه أصح مطلقا وقد خاض به قوم فقيل مالك** عن نافع فيما رواه الناسك مولاه واختر حيث عنه يسند** الشافعي قلت فعنه أحمد
body_en:
Obsessive whispering concerning creed

What is the ruling concerning one who is exposed to Satan's obsessive whisperings in his creed? What is he advised to do?

When a person senses anything of Satan's whispering in what he believes, he must know that this is one of the footsteps of Satan, which God, exalted, has forbidden us to follow, for God, exalted, has said: {O you who believe, do not follow the footsteps of Satan} (Sūrat al-Nūr 24:21). He must make much remembrance of God, exalted, for that drives Satan away. So let him make much seeking of forgiveness, and let him say 'there is no god but God', for this cuts off Satan's path and removes those whisperings entirely. And he must not pursue the thought: if a passing thought comes, he must not turn it over again, but should cut it off with the remembrance of God, exalted...

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

By what are creed and the foundations of religion established?

Are creed and the foundations of religion established by a singly transmitted report (khabar al-āḥād)?

The singly transmitted report is of four types in the usage of the hadith scholars. The first of them is the widespread (mustafīḍ), which comes close to the mass-transmitted (mutawātir); separating the two is laborious. By this, creedal doctrines are established without disagreement. The second is the well-known (mashhūr), which is what a number narrated in every layer, not exceeding ten and not falling below three or four. Next to it is the strong (ʿazīz), which is what two or three alone narrated in one of the layers. Next to it is the singular (gharīb), which is what one narrator alone narrated in one layer, in whichever of its layers that may be.

Over these three, people differed as to whether they yield certainty or not. The majority of the legal theorists held that a singly transmitted report, whether well-known, strong or singular, does not yield certainty. The verifying scholars among them held that it does yield certainty if it is attended by indications that point to it. Others held that it yields certainty absolutely, and this is narrated from the majority of the hadith scholars. But the correct position is that singly transmitted reports, if they are attended by indications, do yield certainty; and the hadith scholars give as their example of this what Malik narrates from Nafi from Ibn Umar from the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, for it yields certainty on account of the indications attending it.

On this disagreement, they differed over taking singly transmitted reports as evidence in creedal doctrines. Creedal doctrines divide into two kinds: what certainty is required in, namely the foundations of the creeds and of the religions; and what certainty is not required in, namely their details — such as the details of the attributes of God, glorified and exalted, and the like. The details of the attributes, on the stronger view, do not have certainty as a condition, and therefore singly transmitted reports are accepted in them. So it is possible for an attribute to be established for God, mighty and majestic, by a singly transmitted report, and it is possible for a name to be established for Him by that.

That is why al-Suyuti, may God have mercy on him, says: *His names, glorified be He, are fixed by revelation; a third position holds it of the name only, not of the attribute. And a single instance suffices, and the verbal noun, and the verb, and the suppositions, in the view of the one whose opinion counts.* 'The suppositions' means singly transmitted reports.

As for matters of certainty, and the foundations — the foundations of the religions — certainty is indispensable in them. So on the view that a singly transmitted report yields certainty absolutely, there is no difficulty in their being established by it. And on the view that it yields certainty if attended by indications, the same holds — as with what al-Bukhari narrated in the Ṣaḥīḥ, or what Muslim narrated in the Ṣaḥīḥ: even if it were singular or strong, there attend it such indications as require certainty about it. And if certainty is stipulated in them, then a singly transmitted report is not taken in them.

Our ruling of soundness on what is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs is not intended as certainty in the view of the legal theorists; it is intended as certainty only in the view of the hadith scholars. That is why al-Iraqi, may God have mercy on him, said in the Alfiyyah on hadith terminology: *By 'sound' and 'weak' they intended [a judgement] on the outward, not certainty; and what is relied upon is our refraining from ruling of any chain that it is the soundest absolutely. Some people have ventured upon it, and it was said: Malik, from Nafi, the client of the devout one, in what the latter narrated. And choose, where it is given with a chain from him, al-Shafi'i; I said: and from him, Ahmad.*

flags.arabic: و ليقل \"لا إله إلا الله\" فهذا يقطع على الشيطان السبيل
flags.context: the first item, where the quotation marks around the formula carry literal backslashes
options: preserve the backslashes in body_ar and drop them from body_en (done here)
strip the backslashes from body_ar as well
flags.note: CMS ESCAPING ARTIFACT (style guide §11). The stored record carries literal backslashes before the quotation marks, an addslashes artifact. They are preserved in body_ar and omitted from body_en. This is corpus-wide and should be cleaned globally rather than per record; it is recorded here so the global pass can be verified against a known instance.

flags.arabic: أسماؤه سبحانه موقفة** ثالثها الاسم فقط دون الصفه / ويكتفى بمرة والمصدر** والفعل والظنون في المعتبر
flags.context: al-Suyuti's two lines on whether the divine names are fixed by revelation
options: render as prose in italics, reading موقفة as tawqīfiyyah, 'fixed by revelation'
render as prose, reading موقفة as mawqūfah, 'suspended/held back'
leave the verse untranslated and carry only the Sheikh's gloss
flags.note: موقفة as printed is metrically convenient but is not the usual form; the question the line answers is the standard one of whether the divine names are tawqīfī (established only by revealed text). The reading affects the sense directly. Note also that ثالثها ('a third of them') signals a third position in a list of positions that the Sheikh does not enumerate here, so the line is elliptical without al-Suyuti's surrounding text.

flags.arabic: فقيل مالك عن نافع فيما رواه الناسك مولاه
flags.context: al-Iraqi's lines on the soundest chain of transmission
options: Malik, from Nafi, the client of the devout one, in what the latter narrated
Malik, from Nafi, in what the devout one narrated — his client [being Nafi]
Malik, from Nafi, the client of the devout one who narrated it
flags.note: The line compresses the golden chain al-Shafi'i ← Malik ← Nafi ← Ibn Umar. الناسك ('the devout one') is Ibn Umar and مولاه ('his client') is Nafi, but the two words are separated across the hemistich break, so the English has to choose how to attach them. The chain itself is unambiguous; only the phrasing is.

flags.arabic: وهو الذي رواه عدد في كل طبقة لا يزيدون على العشرة ولا ينقصون عن الثلاثة أو الأربعة
flags.context: the Sheikh's numerical definition of the well-known (mashhūr) report
options: render the numbers exactly as given, including the 'three or four' hesitation
render as 'at least three' and note the variant
flags.note: The lower bound is given as 'three or four', which is the Sheikh hesitating aloud rather than a fixed definition; the standard definition of mashhūr sets the minimum at three. The hesitation has been kept in the English rather than resolved, since these thresholds are exactly what a reader will take from the passage.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

Two separate fatwas are published on this one page, divided in the source by a rule of hyphens. The rule is preserved in both body_ar and body_en; the site should render them as two separate items. Each item's own heading is part of the source text and has been kept.
The first item breaks off with an ellipsis in the source ('بذكر الله تعالى...'). The ellipsis has been reproduced; it is not a truncation introduced in extraction.
The source repeats a word in the first item ('أن لا يتبع التفكير التفكير'). The repetition is kept in the Arabic and rendered once in the English, which is how it reads.

The lines of verse from al-Suyuti and from al-Iraqi's Alfiyyah are rendered as prose in italics per house style; the source marks the hemistich break with a double asterisk in some lines only. The Arabic should be displayed alongside, since the subject matter is technical terminology.

The Sheikh distinguishes his own position ('the correct position') from the majority of the legal theorists, the verifiers among them, and the majority of the hadith scholars. All four attributions have been kept distinct in the English.
Source spelling preserved verbatim in body_ar: الإستغفار with a connecting hamza, and الصفه written with a final hāʾ for the rhyme.
